title: Naturality of raw truncation maps for one derived morphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] admitting derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For bounded-below complexes $K,N$ and any $c:QK\to QN$, the raw truncation objects and maps [def-sp-truncation-couple] admit maps $t_D^{p,q},t_E^{p,q}$ commuting with $\alpha,f,g$. They also commute with the canonical maps $D^{0,n}\to H^n(RF(QK))$ induced by the truncation inclusion and with the explicit shift comparisons $E^{p,q}\cong H^p(RF(H^q(K)[0]))$ for every integer $p$. In the latter square use the cohomology map of $c$ transported through homologyFunctorFactors. No exactness, bound, invertibility of the abutment maps, or choices for a family of objects are asserted. Exact Lean interface:
theorem raw_naturality (K N : CochainComplex.Plus A)
    (c : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj N.obj) :
    ∃ (tD : ∀ p q : ℤ, D F K p q ⟶ D F N p q)
      (tE : ∀ p q : ℤ, E F K p q ⟶ E F N p q),
      (∀ p q : ℤ, tD p q ≫ alpha F N p q =
        alpha F K p q ≫ tD (p - 1) (q + 1)) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, tE p q ≫ f F N p q = f F K p q ≫ tD (p + 2) (q - 1)) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, tD p q ≫ g F N p q = g F K p q ≫ tE p q) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, tD 0 n ≫ abutmentMap F N n = abutmentMap F K n ≫
        (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map c) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, tE p q ≫ (singleIso F N p q).hom = (singleIso F K p q).hom ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B p).map (homologyMap c q))

proof.text: Descend tau<=q and H^q(-)[-q] along Q. At K,N define maps by conjugating the localization lift maps with fac. Apply RF, H^(p+q), and conjugate by the bridge to define tD,tE. The construction is independent of the proof that the functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms, by proof irrelevance.

Apply the three squares of truncation_triangle to c. The first gives the alpha square at q+1, the second gives g at q, and the boundary square gives f at q via homologySequenceδ_naturality after RF.mapTriangle. Adjacent bridge factors cancel. Equality transports in total degree and truncation index commute with these maps by eqToHom_naturality.

Descend the natural truncation inclusion tau<=n -> identity with liftNatTrans. Its naturality at c, conjugated by fac, is truncMap(c,n);Q(ι_N)=Q(ι_K);c. Apply RF and H^n, cancel bridge factors and the zero total-degree transport; this is the abutment equation. No invertibility of the inclusion is needed.

The single-functor shift comparison, RF shift comparison, and homology shift comparison form a natural isomorphism of functors on A. Apply its naturality to homologyMap(c,q). The descended single-cohomology functor is identified with H^q followed by singleFunctor via homologyFunctorFactors, so its conjugated map is singleFunctor.map(homologyMap(c,q)). Cancel bridge factors to obtain the E equation.
